author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Hierarchy-canonicalizing dependency kinds bypass every cycle detector: mutual child_of edges leave the graph provably inconsistent while validate, health, and graph analyze all report acyclic

The relationship registry canonicalizes several dependency-row kinds to hierarchy edges, but cycle detection only covers ordering kinds, so a hierarchy cycle built from dependency rows is invisible to every check.

Live reproduction on 2026.7.25 in an isolated sandbox workspace with two Task items X and Y:

  pm update X --dep "id=Y,kind=child_of"   -> rc 0
  pm update Y --dep "id=X,kind=child_of"   -> rc 0
  pm validate --json  -> lifecycle status ok, dependency cycle count 0
  pm graph analyze    -> acyclic true, cycle_count 0, cycles []
  pm graph audit      -> edges_by_kind {parent: 2} (both rows canonicalized to hierarchy)
  pm graph ancestors X   -> [Y]
  pm graph descendants X -> [Y]

Y is reported as both an ancestor and a descendant of X. Traversal terminates (visited-set protected) but ancestor/descendant closure, dominators, critical path, and any topological ordering are unsound on that subgraph, and no command discloses it.

The scalar parent field is protected: pm-8vul shipped hierarchy-cycle detection for it and parent ids remain fail-fast at mutation time. The dependency-row channel is not, so there are two hierarchy write paths with asymmetric protection. pm-6irg narrowed the lifecycle cycle check to ordering kinds only to stop related-edge false positives; that fix is correct for associative edges but left the hierarchy-canonicalizing kinds uncovered. pm-i6pi closed the same class for blocked_by, where the failure was a visible pm next deadlock rather than a silent one.

This is reachable by ordinary agents: kind=epic and kind=task are accepted spellings that canonicalize to hierarchy edges, so a plausible mistake by an agent naming a relationship after an item type silently rewrites the hierarchy that pm graph traverses while the parent scalar stays null. In a fleet, dependency rows merge by set union, so two agents on separate branches can each add one sound hierarchy edge that composes into a cycle only after the merge, with no gate that fails.

Cycle detection covers every dependency kind the relationship registry canonicalizes to a hierarchy edge, not only the ordering kinds, and a mutation that would close such a cycle fails fast with the same contract the scalar parent field already enforces; A regression test asserts no item can be reported as both an ancestor and a descendant of the same item by pm graph, for every accepted kind spelling in the declared dependency-kind domain; validate lifecycle, pm health, and pm graph analyze agree on cycle count for a corpus whose cycles are built from dependency rows rather than the parent scalar; The related-edge false-cycle behaviour fixed under pm-6irg does not regress: the reciprocal-related and all-related-loop corpus stays green; Hierarchy cycles already stored on terminal items are reported as legacy findings with their holders named, and are never repaired by mutating closed items; The post-merge composition case is covered: a randomized branch pair that each add one sound hierarchy edge and merge into a cycle fails the merge conformance suite
